highlights.title: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
highlights.summary: I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.
body: Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now.

highlights.summary: One of Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s strangest random encounters occurs when you’re offering taxi services, and a man with a beard wearing a dark suit and sunglasses climbs into the backseat with a gun.
body: Jason or Lucia gets a better deal than Mann’s cabbie in this Easter egg. If you take the stranger to his destination and follow him inside after he takes out some of the criminals there, you can find a ton of valuable loot. Most players seem keen on eliminating the stranger rather than keep driving him around. In Collateral, Jamie Foxx’s character, Max, has to spend the whole night driving Cruise’s Vincent around Los Angeles. If you’ve never seen how that goes for him, Collateral is streaming for free on Pluto TV — and it’s a must-watch, especially if you want a movie that has a vibe as wild and crime-filled as GTA 6 ’s.

Max is a cab driver who’s been telling himself for years that the job is temporary. He wants to start his own limo company someday, so when a well-dressed passenger named Vincent (Cruise) offers him $600 to drive him around for the night, it seems like the kind of opportunity that could get him a little closer to quitting. Then a body lands on his cab at their first destination. Vincent has five people to kill before the night is over. Max has just agreed to drive him to all five stops — and he’s already an accomplice.

highlights.title: Inside Nvidia, Not Everyone Is Celebrating Jensen Huang’s Return
highlights.summary: Some saw Huang’s resignation as an opportunity for culture change at the chip giant. “If Jensen comes back, I’m not doing any HR trainings ever again,” one employee said.
body: Jensen Huang received a “hero’s welcome” from employees on Monday after Nvidia’s board of directors reinstated him as CEO, according to people who were present. An outspoken faction of Nvidia’s workforce had demanded his return and greeted him with chants, raucous applause, and hugs at the company’s headquarters.

But other employees were quietly stewing. Several current and former Nvidia staffers had viewed Huang’s abrupt exit earlier this month as a rare opportunity to change the “one team” corporate culture of unfettered unity and minimal bureaucracy that he had cultivated over the past three decades, according to interviews with the workers, as well as internal correspondence and social media posts reviewed by WIRED. Most spoke on the condition of anonymity because they feared backlash from colleagues.

highlights.title: Many languages, one common neural code
highlights.summary: Analyzing speakers of 21 languages, an MIT study using multilingual AI finds the human brain may represent meaning in much the same way.
body: Languages take on thousands of forms. Some are tonal, like Vietnamese, where shifts in pitch convey distinct meanings. English relies on precise word orders, but this matters less for Russian, where words can be swapped without changing the intended message.
Despite so much variety in the linguistic kingdom, an MIT study has found that the human brain may process all sorts of languages in a universal way.

Artificial intelligence made this finding possible. In the study published today in Nature Neuroscience, the researchers used multilingual models to predict how the human brain responds to various languages. Those models also helped the researchers detect a shared brain process across people who collectively spoke 21 different languages.

“Of course, there are many differences in the ways humans converse with each other. But our team found that there is something fundamentally similar in how the brain communicates,” says Evelina Fedorenko, who is an investigator at MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research, an associate professor of brain and cognitive sciences, and the senior author of the paper.

highlights.summary: Clash Royale developer Supercell has recruited the creator of an advanced AI cheating tool to help crack down on cheating in the game.
body: AI cheating has become a growing controversy in Clash Royale, with increasingly sophisticated bots reportedly capable of outperforming skilled human players. Players highlighted claims that an AI-controlled account named ‘Clasher’ had reached the top of the game’s global leaderboard.

The situation prompted calls for Supercell to intervene, with the developer addressing the controversy on November 20. In a statement posted on X, Clash Royale warned that using AI or other tools to cheat was a “royal crime,” declaring that offending players would be banished from the Arena.
On November 21, the official Clash Royale X account announced that it had caught the creator of an AI cheating tool and recruited them to help develop new anti-cheat technology.

“The creator of the AI cheating tool has been caught,” Supercell announced in a statement framed as a royal decree from the King. “He’s agreed, entirely of his own free will, to join forces with the Clash Royale team.

highlights.summary: Anthropic is launching some new Claude AI features to help software engineers ship code. As part of a new Claude Ship product being announced today, Claude now can review, fix, and approve pull requests.
body: Anthropic is bringing new AI tools to software engineers with Claude Ship.

Engineers have already been able to take advantage of Claude’s code review capabilities thanks to the Code Review feature, which was announced in March and became generally available in October. What’s new alongside Claude Ship are the PR Steward and Claude Approvals agents, which are launching in beta today.

PR Steward “jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members” and leaves comments on what it changed, according to Anthropic. Claude Approvals can approve routine changes if an organization’s policy allows it. “Teams can have Claude Approvals consider a variety of signals in its decision-making process, including Code Review findings or their own classifiers using natural language,” Anthropic says.
Claude Ship is now available for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and works with repositories on GitHub.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang Is Back, and So Is Nvidia’s Stock
highlights.summary: Jensen Huang comes back, numbers go up. Maybe the reason behind the CEO’s return is just that simple?
body: The chipmaker’s shares have surged more than 30 percent following the board’s announcement that it was reinstating Huang as president, CEO, and board member. The company’s valuation has soared by more than $1 trillion, which puts it on track to break Microsoft’s record for the greatest single-day gain in market value by hundreds of billions of dollars.

Huang departed the company he helped found on November 12 amid suspected asset-kissing and allegations of extramarital affairs with employees. Each report chipped away at the company’s value until nearly $2.2 trillion was erased over the past month.

Last week, board chair Harvey Jones said during the company’s earnings call that the board did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” WIRED also reported that Nvidia’s board had been alarmed by Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying.”

And yet, despite all this, the board announced on Monday that it had brought Huang back— with some help from the US government. Semafor reported that, hours before Huang was reinstated, President Donald Trump dialed into the publicly traded company’s board meeting to argue for the ousted CEO’s return.

highlights.summary: Week 11 of the 2026 NFL regular season wrapped up on Monday Night Football with the Cincinnati Bengals visiting Northwest Stadium to take on the Washington Commanders under the lights… except for a few brief moments.
body: During the third quarter, there was a power outage at the stadium, and it went completely pitch black.
Some quick-thinking fans attempted to light up the venue with their cellphones, but that was obviously not enough. Joe Buck even got in a wise-crack about the entertaining sight.

Later in the broadcast, Buck revealed the actual reason for the power outage, and it was a reason so ridiculous you couldn’t make it up. As it turns out, they forgot that Monday Night Football was on Monday night.

“If you want to know the reason why the lights went out earlier, the official word is the lighting vendor never disabled the regularly scheduled maintenance for 10 p.m.,” Buck said. “It’s a weekday thing, and they forgot it was a Monday night game.”

highlights.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing.
body: Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.

This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll, 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).

But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.

highlights.summary: Megha Ganne won the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying stage as 27 tour cards were claimed for the 2027 season, with five-time USA Solheim Cup team member Megan Khang among those successful.
body: Khang - part of Team USA for the past five Solheim Cups - is returning to the LPGA Tour, on which she's made 259 starts since 2016, winning the 2023 CPKC Women's Open.
The top-25 finishers and ties at the conclusion of the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying were awarded LPGA Tour status for next year.

American Ganne won the final stage outright on 23 under, one shot clear of Shannon Tan and Julia Gregg in a tie for second. Min Sun7 Kim was fourth on 21 under and Xiaowen Yin one further back in fifth.
Ganne, the 2025 US Amateur champion, had actually already secured her 2027 LPGA Tour status by entering the week by finishing 11-15 on the Epson Tour.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Was Biggest Launch in PlayStation History
highlights.summary: Now that the dust has somewhat settled after the avalanche that was the launch of GTA 6, PlayStation has revealed some of its stats from the game, revealing that this was the single largest game release in PlayStation history.
body: PlayStation’s November 23 blog post states that more than 39 million unique players have played the game on the PlayStation 5, setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any PlayStation game. This beats out other records for multiplayer games, single-player games, and perhaps most astonishingly, even free-to-play titles.

On top of that, GTA 6 players logged a total of 683 million hours played in the game, with the average player spending an estimated 17.4 hours sticking up virtual pawn shops and stealing NPC’s cars during its first few days.

What’s more impressive is the sheer amount of people who purchased PS5s specifically to play GTA 6. PlayStation’s blog says it saw the “largest number of newly-connected PS5 consoles on a single day” since the console’s launch in November 2020, not counting end-of-year holidays like Christmas. Since GTA 6’s launch, it was the first game played on 70% of these new consoles.

GTA 6 has, perhaps unsurprisingly, broken a slew of big records. The most prominent of these is its status as the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with Rockstar reporting that the game earned $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours.

highlights.title: On Location: Dig Stars Amy Poehler and Geraldine Viswanathan on Italian Gelato, Go-Karting—and Tailgating
highlights.summary: The 10-part Peacock series set on an Greek archaeological site found its muse in Italy’s Puglia region.
body: On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television shows, and more. This time, we take a look at Dig.

Amy Poehler had never been to Greece, but she was immediately entranced by Kate Myers’s novel Excavations about four women coming together for an archaeological dig in Athens. So she took her first trip there to set the scene for her 10-part Peacock comedy series Dig, which drops November 23.

“The way in which Greek people mingle with real antiquities every day, walking past very important structures, is archaeology in process,” the Saturday Night Live alum tells Traveler. “The old and the new are constantly bumping up against each other. It was very cool to be there and really helped remind us of the theme of the show that the past is just around the corner and you can't hide from it.”
